primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic nephropathy (advanced diabetic kidney disease) – CKD stage 4
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily; titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5 mg then 10 mg as tolerated to achieve BP <140/90 mmHg
medications.purpose: Control hypertension and reduce proteinuria to slow CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; monitor creatinine & potassium after dose changes

medications.purpose: Slow CKD progression and provide cardiovascular protection, usable down to eGFR 20 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends SGLT2 inhibitor (TA775) for CKD with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m² or albuminuria

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD stage 4) – risk of lactic acidosis (NG203 contraindicated)
contraindications.alternative: Consider basal insulin or GLP‑1 receptor agonist after HbA1c assessment

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention (NG203 contraindicated in CKD stage 4)
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for pain; avoid NSAIDs

contraindications.reason: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury (NG203 contraindicated)
contraindications.alternative: Use either ACE‑I (Ramipril) OR ARB (Losartan) if ACE‑I intolerant

contraindications.reason: Nephrotoxic, especially in advanced CKD (NG203 contraindicated)
contraindications.alternative: Use alternative mood stabiliser; monitor renal function closely

contraindications.reason: High risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy when eGFR <30 (NG203 contraindicated)
contraindications.alternative: If imaging required, use low‑osmolar contrast with hydration and N‑acetylcysteine prophylaxis

assumptions_warnings: Exact eGFR value not provided – assumed CKD stage 4 (eGFR 15‑29 mL/min/1.73 m²) for dosing decisions
Serum potassium, liver function tests, and QRISK score not available – baseline labs required before initiating Ramipril and Atorvastatin
Albumin‑creatinine ratio (ACR) not documented – assumed microalbuminuria present given diagnosis
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or SGLT2 inhibitor allergies before prescribing
HbA1c and detailed diabetes medication history missing – glycaemic management plan pending lab results
treatment_summary: Start ramipril (ACE‑I) to control BP and reduce proteinuria, add dapagliflozin to slow CKD progression, and initiate atorvastatin for cardiovascular risk reduction. Avoid metformin, chronic NSAIDs, dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy, lithium, and unprotected IV contrast. Baseline labs (eGFR, potassium, LFTs, ACR, HbA1c) are required before initiation, with regular monitoring per NG203.
